chapter: Regional bands, politics and travel abroad
title: Living with the Johnson brothers and coming east with Benny Carter
summary: Wilson says he, Budd and Keg lived in Mrs. Potter's rooming house and he felt like a third Johnson brother; Carter took Keg, not Budd.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I can remember Bud Johnson coming into Chicago out of Kansas City. (Inaudible) in Chicago.

Bud and Keg and I, we lived in Mrs. Potter's rooming house on South Parkway. We were almost like brothers. I was one of the Johnson Brothers for a long time. Because Keg and I came to New York together with Benny Carter. And we were so disappointed because Benny didn't bring Bud. But he already had Johnny Russell, a great tenor player here.
That's right. A great tenor player. Ben Webster liked him a lot, too.
Liked Johnny Russell? Yeah, nice guy. Benny Carter liked him and that's why he didn't bring Bud.
But Budd later came, I guess.
